title: What ICT order blocks actually are (in 5 images)
caption: Order blocks are the most drawn, least understood concept in trading. Five images that finally make it click. Save this and stop guessing your zones.

promptVars.SERIES: What ICT order blocks actually are
promptVars.CONCEPT: An order block is the last opposing candle before an explosive move
promptVars.VISUAL: A clean minimal candlestick chart, one red candle highlighted with a glowing box right before a large green impulse leg, premium financial-graphic style, near-black background

promptVars.SERIES: What ICT order blocks actually are
promptVars.CONCEPT: Big players couldn't fill all size at once — unfilled orders remain in that zone
promptVars.VISUAL: A clean illustration of a large glowing block with partial-fill bars inside it, small remaining-liquidity dots still pulsing, premium minimal financial style, near-black background

promptVars.SERIES: What ICT order blocks actually are
promptVars.CONCEPT: Price retraces back into the order block to fill remaining orders, then continues
promptVars.VISUAL: A candlestick path that rallies, curves back down to tap a highlighted zone box, then resumes upward — a clean arrow tracing the move, premium financial graphic, near-black background

promptVars.SERIES: What ICT order blocks actually are
promptVars.CONCEPT: Lower-timeframe order blocks are noise — only higher-timeframe ones hold weight
promptVars.VISUAL: Three stacked timeframe panels labeled D1, H4, M5 — the D1 and H4 zones glowing solid, the M5 one faded and crossed out, clean premium hierarchy graphic, near-black background

promptVars.SERIES: What ICT order blocks actually are
promptVars.CONCEPT: The zone is not a signal — you wait for a market structure shift inside it
promptVars.VISUAL: A highlighted zone box with price entering it, then a clean break-of-structure arrow snapping the opposite way with a bold checkmark, premium financial minimal, near-black background
